chi_tiet.mo_ta:
The Pacific Ocean is a vast world of giants and deep sea creatures. Witness the ecosystems that shape our planet.

The Pacific Ocean spans across our planet, hosting everything from sunlight-filled coral reefs to volcanic activity beneath the waves. This footage captures the scale of this environment, observing the giants like whales and the resilience of marine life that thrives in these waters.

Beneath the surface, the environment shifts to include extreme landscapes where lava flows meet the sea. By examining these diverse ocean ecosystems, we gain a clearer understanding of the forces that sustain life in the largest body of water on Earth. From the deep sea creatures adapted to pressure to the giants navigating the open currents, every aspect of this habitat tells a story of survival.

chi_tiet.tieu_de: Coral Sea: How Currents, Seamounts And Reefs Connect An Ocean | Marine Life Documentary
chi_tiet.mo_ta:
The Coral Sea stretches east of Queensland across an enormous expanse of the western Pacific, from shallow tropical reefs to deep ocean habitats approaching 6,000 metres.

In this documentary, we explore the currents, coral reefs, remote islands, seamounts, canyons, and deep-water ecosystems that make the Coral Sea far more than a tropical reef environment.

The Coral Sea Marine Park protects nearly one million square kilometres of ocean. Beneath its surface, the Tasmantid Seamount Chain extends for roughly 2,000 kilometres, with ancient volcanic mountains rising thousands of metres above the surrounding seafloor.

In 2025, Australia's RV Investigator surveyed deep habitats between roughly 200 and 3,600 metres. By April 2026, more than 120 fish and invertebrate species from the expedition had been identified as new to science, with further discoveries expected as specimens are examined.

The surface is changing too. During the 2025–26 wet season, sea-surface temperatures in the Coral Sea were the warmest on record for a second consecutive season, around 0.99°C above the 1961–1990 average.
